A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M4-SAR, MSRODet and E2E-OSDet, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. Inspection includes all supplementary material in v3; substantial portions match material moved from v2's main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection benchmarks, module ablations and OGSOD-1.0/2.0 experiments in Tables II-IV, alongside qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original detection benchmarks and ablations in Tables 2-3, retains OGSOD experiments in Appendix 10.5 and Table 4, and adds alignment measurements and qualitative results.

M1.justification: FAM, interleaved CMIM, AFM and the composite detection loss are retained. Although v3 explicitly adds residual feature terms to the AFM equation, those connections already appear in v2's Figure 4 and accompanying description; this supports a clarification rather than a changed architecture.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same six-category M4-SAR dataset and OGSOD-1.0/2.0. M4-SAR retains 112,174 image pairs, its acquisition conditions and resolution/polarization coverage. Additional alignment measurements and visual examples examine existing coverage rather than introduce new datasets or test environments.

E2.justification: The M4-SAR comparison adds YOLO26 and YOLO-Master in both single-source settings and MHFNet for fusion, while removing Roi-Trans, KFIoU and E2E-MFD. MHFNet also replaces E2E-MFD in qualitative comparisons. The timing comparison additionally includes COMO and YOLOv12, already evaluated elsewhere in v2. OGSOD comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds FLOPs as a computational metric in Table 2 and MSE, SSIM and mutual information for the alignment assessment in Figure 3(d). Existing detection metrics, training budgets and input resolutions remain unchanged. The newly specified YOLOv11-S variant and FP16 training are additional disclosures, not established setting changes.

E4.justification: v3 adds a weak-alignment analysis in Section 2.5, expands handcrafted-feature SSIM examples in Figure 12, and revises and expands detection and attention case studies in Figures 7-8 and 13-14. The module ablation table and filter, scanning, feature-proportion and attention-area sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experiments. The added alignment and SSIM measurements are descriptive results rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Localized numerical revisions include optical O-RepPoint mAP changing from 53.9 to 26.7 and optical LSKNet from 53.9 to 34.0 in Table II/2, without an explanation. Comparator results, FLOPs, timing entries and additional qualitative/SSIM results are added or removed. New alignment scores are MSE 0.0662, SSIM 0.1256 and MI 0.1729. E2E-OSDet's 61.4 M4-SAR mAP, ablations and OGSOD scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix 9, Equation 8 revises AFM's inputs from the enhanced features alone to their sums with the original features. This corrects the formal expression in v2 Equation 10 to match the residual connections already depicted. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract changes 'precisely aligned' pairs to 'instance-level aligned' pairs. The introduction replaces claimed superiority in alignment precision with superiority in image numbers and drops the explicit claim of improved inference speed. The dataset, toolkit and framework contributions, including the abstract's 5.7% fusion-gain claim, remain.

C2.justification: v2 chiefly qualifies alignment through temporal discrepancies affecting dynamic targets. v3 makes coarse geographic registration a central challenge and explicitly excludes applications requiring precise pixel alignment, including registration and pixel-level fusion (Sections 2.5 and 5.1). Section 4.4 also introduces method-specific interpretations of mislocalization and robustness under modal shifts. These substantially revise the dataset's applicability boundaries and interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds normalized quadrilateral annotation formats, category IDs and dataset directory organization in Appendix 7. It names ENVI and discloses the Ultralytics implementation, shared YOLOv11-S backbone/neck and FP16 training in Section 2.3 and Appendix 10.1. Existing hardware, principal hyperparameters and the project access link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including MHFNet, YOLO-Master, UnravelNet and localized background-aware generative distillation, and removes references including KFIoU and Oriented R-CNN. The main related-work discussion is largely retained in Appendix 8. Renumbering and preprint-to-publication updates do not constitute additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work and detailed method descriptions move into Appendices 8-9, the main method section is condensed, and the OGSOD discussion moves to Appendix 10.5. Dataset analysis and limitations are rewritten, with new supplementary sections for dataset documentation and experimental explanations.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with redrawn construction and architecture diagrams. The ablation and detector-comparison graphics replace 3D/radar displays with bar charts. v3 adds a registration panel, a FLOPs column, annotation illustrations and expanded qualitative panels, removes Table 1's polarization column, and relocates existing displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves documentation of alignment limits, annotation formats and implementation, and provides additional qualitative evidence. However, Table 2 removes E2E-MFD, v2's strongest fusion comparator at 60.5 mAP, while E2E-OSDet remains at 61.4. It also substantially changes two optical baseline result rows without explanation. These documentation gains coexist with reduced comparative evidence and unresolved result revisions, preventing a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
